title: Roadmap Dependency Contingency Buckets & Automated Trigger Policy
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: Roadmap delivery is frequently derailed by late-breaking cross-team blockers (kernel compatibility, design signoff, security gating). We need a prescriptive, automated way to reserve contingency for dependent work, quantify impact, and trigger mitigation policies when thresholds are hit.

Goal: Define a set of contingency buckets (time and engineering FTE equivalents) for roadmap dependencies, a machine-readable trigger policy (based on percent-of-work-blocked and days-of-delay), and a lightweight escalation/runbook that teams can opt into. The system should integrate with Linear statuses and our roadmap dashboard to surface risks and automatically enqueue compensating work (delay buffers, canary-disable switches, or fallback model variants).
acceptance_criteria: Contingency buckets defined: None/Small/Medium/Large with numeric thresholds (days, % effort) and suggested mitigations
Automated trigger policy implemented as a Linear label + webhook that flags impacted milestones when thresholds exceeded
Runbook published to Confluence with playbook steps for PM/Eng/Design/Security
Dashboard tile in Console roadmap view showing active contingency consumption per initiative
Two pilot initiatives (runtime-1.18 and console-2026.04) use the policy for one cycle and report outcomes
tasks: Draft contingency bucket definitions and mapping to mitigations (PM)
Specify webhook payload and Linear label conventions for triggers (Eng)
Design UX for dashboard tile and risk signal (Design)
Security review of automated escalation flow and links to audit logs (Security)
Implement webhook consumer service to update initiative state and enqueue compensations (Eng)
Run two-cycle pilot and capture metrics (time-to-resolution, % of mitigations used) (PM+Eng)
decisions: Use percentage-of-dependent-work and average blocking-duration as dual triggers (agreed 2026-02-25)
Contingency buckets will be configurable per-project but default to org-recommended thresholds to avoid negotiation overhead
Mitigations prioritized: (1) automatic fallback to compatible model variant, (2) temporary capacity shifts from Dedicated pools, (3) UI feature gating in Console
We will surface contingency consumption in the Console roadmap and not modify core SLAs automatically; final gating decisions remain human in-the-loop
